evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:99,116,138-191,406-416 - the long-lived rotating REFRESH token is persisted in localStorage (REFRESH_TOKEN_KEY='ppt_refresh_token') and read back in refreshTokenInternal to send in the request body. localStorage is readable by any JS on the origin, so a single XSS yields the refresh token = full renewable session hijack that survives logout.

Comment at AuthContext.tsx:116 flags it as an MVP shortcut ('localStorage for MVP, httpOnly cookies later'). The migration is now unblocked: api-server already ships httpOnly refresh-cookie support (backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth/mod.rs build_refresh_cookie, Secure/SameSite). The SPA keeps its own localStorage copy and body-passes the token, defeating the backend's httpOnly mechanism.

Fix (security, medium): migrate refresh path to the backend httpOnly cookie - stop persisting refresh token in localStorage; POST /auth/refresh with withCredentials and drop refreshToken from the body. Access token may stay in memory/localStorage. No backend change needed (capability exists). Confidence medium: static-confirmed persistence + helper existence; did not runtime-verify the endpoint sets the cookie for the SPA caller.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:86-101 - buildWebSocketUrl() puts the full access JWT in the URL query string (url.searchParams.set('token', token) -> wss://host/ws/notifications?token=<jwt>). The JWT then lands in api-server access logs, any reverse-proxy/CDN logs, APM/trace spans, and browser history; a leaked JWT is a usable bearer credential until expiry.
The code documents the real browser constraint (no Authorization header on WS handshake) but does not mitigate the log/history leakage of the bearer token in the query string.

Fix (security, low): replace the in-URL access JWT with a short-lived single-use WS ticket - a POST /auth/ws-ticket returning an opaque ~30s one-time token placed in ?ticket=, exchanged server-side at handshake. Lower priority than the refresh-token finding since the access token is short-lived. Confidence medium: static-confirmed; actual log retention depends on deploy infra.
